analysis.answer: Currently, cities can adopt their own ordinances regulating the sale and possession of firearms. The measure changes this by establishing complete state preemption, voiding any existing city firearm ordinances and preventing cities from passing new ones.

The measure addresses the existence of varying local firearm restrictions, which can create a fragmented legal landscape for those selling or carrying firearms across municipal lines. The mechanism eliminates this patchwork by voiding all city-level regulations, ensuring that only uniform state laws apply.

The state legislature gains exclusive control over firearm policy, while city governments lose the discretion to tailor firearm rules to local conditions. Individuals and businesses involved in the sale or possession of firearms benefit by no longer having to navigate or comply with varying local municipal ordinances.
